title: POC weekly sync — model armoring & rollback rehearsal

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-19 14:00 PT · Duration 46 min · Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Tom Berger (Redwood CSM), Carlos Medina (BlueWave HMOps), Priya Kapoor (Lead ML Eng), Lena Ortiz (Security), Samir Nadeem (SRE).

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, we'll try to keep tight, main agenda — pick the armored model set for pilot traffic and rehearse the rollback steps. Maya will go over the latency numbers first.
[01:14] Maya: cool yeah, hi all. quick note, these are bench numbers from our last stagerun, the file is at: S3 link (bench_q_variants.csv) — quick caveat transcription might read that link weird. so, we tested q4-int8, q5-int8 and q4-fp16. q4-int8 average 80ms token at 512 tokens, tail (p99) ~420ms; q5-int8 average 72ms, p99 ~510ms — oh yeah p99 was higher for q5 likely because memory juggling and kernel path.
[03:00] Priya: wait q5 p99 higher but avg lower? is that measurement noise or workload skew? we saw something similar during our spikes.
[03:22] Maya: yeah that was my note, the p95/p99 were sensitive to sequence length variance and batching thresholds. we suspect the allocator path on our newer cu kernel for q5 triggers an occasional GC-ish stall.
[03:41] Samir: GC-ish? do you mean KV cache eviction or CUDA mem compaction?
[03:47] Maya: more like kernel blocking while moving KV pages, so it looks like a micro-sched hiccup. may be mitigated with our tiled-kv patch but that patch isn't in the q5 build we tested.
[04:12] Carlos: so does that mean if we pick q5 for better average cost we risk occasional spikes that breach our 300ms SLO?
[04:24] Maya: yes, possible. with canary thresholds at 0.1% traffic we didn't see p99 blowouts, but at 5–10% traffic p99 became more apparent.
[04:40] Jordan: important for the decision: BlueWave's customer experience KPI flags at 300ms so we should pick the variant that minimizes p99 while meeting cost targets. what do we think about pinning q4-int8 as primary with q5 as soft-fallback for cost bursts?
[05:02] Priya: that was my leaning — q4-int8 seemed steadier. but I want to be sure the catalog names map correctly to our infra; we had a mismatch last week where "redwood-q4-v2" pointed to an older shard.
[05:22] Maya: yep, catalog reconciliation is a must. we propose to canonicalize model refs with both digest and friendly tag: e.g., redwood/q4@sha256:xxxx and redwood/q4:staging-20270812. that'll let you pin by digest to avoid drift.
[05:46] Lena: from a security/audit perspective we need to capture swap events in audit logs and ensure KMS signatures for any pinned digest changes. can you describe how a rollback would be recorded?
[06:02] Maya: good Q. our platform emits an event to the audit stream on every deployment change — fields include old_digest, new_digest, operator, reason. logs go to your SIEM via the forwarding connector. we can toggle retention to 13 months for enterprise pilot.
[06:22] Lena: perfect, we may ask for an attestation template for legal to sign off on record retention.
[06:29] Tom: I'll add that as a follow-up item.
[06:35] [07:02] Jordan: let's role-play a rollback rehearsal — Maya you'll run through the steps and Samir/Priya will confirm they can execute them from staging.
[07:14] Maya: step one: detect via canary alert when latency threshold cross >0.5% of requests over 500ms for 3m. step two: trigger automated soft-fallback policy which routes traffic above percentile to the pinned stable variant. step three: if soft-fallback doesn't resolve, run the rollback job which applies a digest pin to route 100% to last-known-good. the rollback job requires two operators in the console or via API with SSO MFA.
[08:02] Priya: wait is there a dry-run mode that doesn't touch production routing but simulates the routing decision? we want to test that decision matrix.
[08:16] Maya: yes we have a 'shadow-route' dry-run that mirrors decision outputs but doesn't change live routing. it produces diffs and a predicted latency distribution. recommend running that in the tabletop first.
[08:34] Samir: how long does the digest pin take to propagate?
[08:38] Maya: propagation is ~12–30s to edge nodes for route table updates and up to 60s for in-flight sessions to drain depending on KV cache TTL. but note: if you have long-lived streaming sessions we recommend a fast cutover with abort+retry logic in the client.
[08:57] Carlos: that 60s drain is important. our streaming agent holds open connections for longer. do you have a suggested client retry pattern?
[09:10] Maya: recommended — detect non-200, then soft-retry once after 500ms, if still fails escalate. for streaming we recommend issuing a short-lived sentinel token to force session refresh on cutover. we'll include code snippet in the runbook.
[09:30] [10:05] Priya: back to catalog mismatch: last week's "redwood-q4-v2" mapping issue — can we add a guard that prevents digest aliasing unless two approvals are present? that would have stopped the drift.
[10:18] Jordan: yes we can enable stricter RBAC for alias updates in pilot orgs. default can be 2-approver policy for alias-to-digest changes.
[10:28] Lena: also can we log the diffs to a signed blob so legal can verify identity of approvers?
[10:33] Maya: we sign diffs and store them in your audit bucket, optional integrity proofs via HSM.
[10:40] Samir: curious: what about fallback variants that are smaller models, like a 'lite' family — if we route to a lite model do we lose quality in critical responses? has BlueWave tested semantic drift?
[10:58] Carlos: we did a small eval, lite models are okay for generic summarization but fail specific clinical tone. our success criteria require clinical fidelity for diagnosis-adjacent prompts.
[11:14] Maya: then fallback policy should be layered: 1) attempt soft-fallback to a compatible quantized full-size variant, 2) if fails, route only non-critical endpoints to lite model, 3) for critical endpoints auto-fail to human-in-the-loop. those rules can be expressed per-route in the console.
[11:41] Priya: per-route control is crucial. can we tag routes as "critical" and lock fallback behavior?
[11:48] Maya: yes that's supported. we'll provide a sample policy for your critical endpoints.
[12:02] [12:58] Jordan: I want to call out cost: q5-int8 saved ~12% token cost in our run, but if p99 breaches cause user-visible errors, that's a wash. so alternative is dynamic hedging: route 90% to q4-int8, 10% to q5-int8 for steady ops and increase q5 share when latency headroom is observed.
[13:20] Priya: interesting, can that be automated? we don't want to babysit percentages.
[13:29] Maya: yes, 'hedging controller' can adjust weights based on observed latency windows. we need to set safe thresholds for CPU/GPU load to avoid oscillation. we can give you the controller config used in our tests.
[13:44] Samir: what observability do we get? token-level breakdown? traces?
[13:50] Maya: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model latency histogram, per-route traces (sampling), and a trace link to the raw request payload if you opt-in. sensitive payloads can be redacted before storing.
[14:08] Lena: redaction is mandatory for us. we need PII scrub rules and retention limits.
[14:14] Maya: noted — we have a PII scrubber that uses deterministic redaction rules and returns a scrub report. we'll attach the data-handling doc.
[14:29] [15:20] Jordan: quick notation — legal asked for a short attestation that rollback operations are logged and immutable for 13 months, and that there's an SLA for rollback assistance for dedicated customers. Tom you'll follow-up?
[15:33] Tom: yep, i'll surface the attestation template and SLA excerpt.
[15:40] Priya: during the stress runs what exact traffic mix did you use for bench? we need to replicate to validate the p99 behavior.
[15:50] Maya: we used a mixed distribution: 60% short prompts (avg 64 tokens), 30% mid (200 tokens), 10% long (600 tokens) with bursting patterns (2x bursts every 5m). config file is linked in the bench CSV.
[16:10] Carlos: okay we'll replay that mix.
[16:18] [17:02] Jordan: let's script the rollback rehearsal: 1) run shadow-route diff, 2) flip 10% traffic to fallback via soft-fallback, 3) monitor SLOs for 15m, 4) execute digest pin to last-known-good if issues persist, 5) capture audit blob. Priya/Samir can you commit to performing steps 1–3 in staging next Tue?
[17:32] Priya: yes we can do that. Samir: yup.
[17:40] Jordan: we'll be on the tabletop; Maya will provide the script.
[17:46] Maya: I'll publish the dry-run script and the runbook to the pilot folder and post link in the CRM thread.
[18:05] [19:00] Carlos: one more question about rollback safety — if the pinned digest points to a model that is not available in the region, do you auto-fallback to region-compatible variant? we had an outage in eu-west where fingerprints didn't line up.
[19:18] Maya: we have region-compatibility checks; if the pinned digest can't be satisfied in region, policy options are: 1) failover to cross-region routing (with latency warning), 2) route to local compatible variant if policy allows, or 3) circuit-break and send 503 to avoid stale predictions. we can set per-route preference.
[19:46] Samir: cross-region has compliance implications for us. we'll likely choose local variant fallback or block.
[19:56] Lena: block unless legal signs cross-region fallback for specific endpoints.
[20:02] Jordan: understood — we'll make those policy defaults explicit in the runbook.
[20:10] [21:35] Tom: quick housekeeping: I'll add the attestation and the bench CSV references to the pilot Confluence page and ping legal.
[21:48] Jordan: ok wrapping up, recap and owners: Jordan share latency CSV (Maya attach config), Maya publish dry-run and runbook, Tom share attestation template, Carlos run staged stress tests, Lena confirm KMS attestation. schedule tabletop for 2027-08-26 10:00 PT.
[22:20] Priya: thanks all, that table-top time works for us.
[22:26] Carlos: thanks.
[22:30] Maya: thanks everyone, I'll also include the hedging controller config and a short note on kernel behavior for q5.
[22:45] [Closing 22:50] Speaker 1: call ended.

Notes and links referenced: bench_q_variants.csv (S3), pilot-runbook-digestpin.md (Redwood console link), legal-attestation-template.pdf (shared drive), dry-run-script.sh (gist link).
